authorizedUse.title: Authorized Security Assessment Policy
authorizedUse.subtitle: Guidelines governing dual-use security tools, laboratory research environments, and responsible assessment practices.
authorizedUse.coreScopingDesc: The software tools cataloged within OBSIDIAN include active network discovery scanners, password strength auditors, directory brute-forcers, and vulnerability verification templates. These instruments are dual-use by design and must be executed strictly against:
authorizedUse.scope1: Localhost infrastructure, container networks, and private virtual machines.
authorizedUse.scope2: Dedicated Capture The Flag (CTF) environments and range simulations.
authorizedUse.scope3: Intentionally vulnerable testbeds (e.g. OWASP Juice Shop, DVWA, Metasploitable).
authorizedUse.scope4: Enterprise systems where explicit written authorization and Rules of Engagement (RoE) are established.
authorizedUse.prohibitedConductDesc: OBSIDIAN does not provide public remote exploitation infrastructure. Documentation is oriented towards defensive understanding, configuration auditing, and remediation. Conducting port sweeps, credential extraction, or vulnerability verification against third-party systems without prior contractual authorization is unlawful and breaches industry ethical standards.
authorizedUse.responsibleDisclosureDesc: When security practitioners discover software vulnerabilities during authorized research, they should follow coordinated disclosure frameworks (such as ISO/IEC 29147 and CERT guidelines), providing maintainers adequate remediation windows prior to public dissemination.

about.title: About {name}
about.missionP1: OBSIDIAN was architected to serve as an authoritative, high-density knowledge and tooling platform for cybersecurity practitioners, digital forensics investigators, SOC analysts, and security researchers.
about.missionP2: Rather than functioning as a passive list of web bookmarks or a decorative simulation, OBSIDIAN provides verified documentation, cross-tool operational workflows, client-side input analysis, and local-first cryptographic utilities designed for rapid operational recall.
about.attributionP1: All external open-source tools, repositories, brand names, and software indexed within the OBSIDIAN catalog belong exclusively to their respective creators, maintainers, and open-source foundations.
about.attributionP2: OBSIDIAN makes no claim of ownership or authorship over third-party software such as Nmap, Volatility, Hashcat, BloodHound, Impacket, or other cataloged utilities. Every tool detail page prominently attributes the canonical upstream repository, license requirements, and official documentation portals.
about.privacyP1: Security analysts routinely evaluate sensitive artifacts including IP addresses, internal domains, hashes, and tokens. OBSIDIAN implements its Universal Technical Analyzer and all native utilities entirely within your local browser runtime. Pasted technical data is never transmitted across the network.
